method: Read each accessible primary full text and compare the note’s abstract, transformed claims, source locators, model or empirical framing, metadata, template, tags, warnings, and preserved reference-link order. For inaccessible full text, audit is limited to publisher abstract/metadata and note the access limit.

Literature/Papers/Entries/RecSim- A Conf.findings: The publisher/arXiv full paper was read, including components and non-objectives (§§1.4, 3.1–3.2). The abstract matches the source. Research questions are supportable. The four model prompts are present; claims that RecSim is a configurable environment rather than one universal user law are accurate and source-located to §§2–3. DOI, date, authors, tags, source and exact preserved reference order/count (58) check out. No substantive issue found.

Literature/Papers/Entries/Reciprocal Rec.findings: The arXiv record and university-hosted publisher PDF were read. Abstract and citation metadata are consistent; 254 original reference links remain in exact order. The note calls this only a literature analysis and has no Model section, but the paper explicitly contributes a general reciprocal recommender conceptual model (Section 2, Fig. 2; formal mutual preference scores p_x,y and p_y,x combined by a fusion function). The extraction omits this model despite the four-question model requirement. The study-design paragraph is otherwise accurate.

Literature/Papers/Entries/Redesigning al.primary_source_read: primary abstract/metadata read; full text inaccessible
Literature/Papers/Entries/Redesigning al.findings: The Nature primary page’s abstract and publication metadata were available; full article text was blocked, consistent with the existing `fulltext unavailable` flag. The note’s study-design paragraph stays within the abstract. The Abstract is not an exact copy: after the publisher abstract it appends the protocol-registration statement and a duplicate summary sentence. DOI, publication date 2026-05-27, authors, tags and 59 preserved reference links check out. Full-text claims remain unverified; LIMITED for those claims.

Literature/Papers/Entries/Reliable and E.findings: The full JASSS PDF was read, including abstract and framework/performance descriptions. The study-design summary correctly distinguishes software/performance evaluation from a substantive behavioral model and reports the comparison and AWS EC2 calibration experiment. Abstract is not exact: words are joined across sentence/word boundaries (e.g. `systems.Over`, `smallscale`), while the publisher PDF has separated words (`systems. Over`, `small-scale`). DOI, publication date, authors, tags and 51 reference links/order check out.

Literature/Papers/Entries/Reranking part.findings: The full Science PDF was read. Abstract matches the paper; study design correctly records preregistration, 1,256 X users, a 10-day experiment and the 2024 campaign, and identifies the randomized exposure intervention and affective-polarization result. This is an empirical field experiment, so no simulation model is claimed. DOI, date, authors, tags, source and all 82 preserved references/order check out.

Literature/Papers/Entries/SARDINE- Simul.findings: The full arXiv paper was read, including the simulator loop (§3), environments (§4), and results (§5). The abstract and high-level aims are accurate, but the model extraction is too generic for the accessible procedure: a session samples a user embedding, presents a recommendation/slate, computes relevance and clicks, updates user embedding for boredom and clicked-item influence when enabled, and repeats to session length; there are fully and partially observable variants and nine environments. Current text says only that nine environments are used and defers to the abstract; it omits the defining step order and user state transitions. DOI/date/source/tags and 63 original reference links in order check out.

Literature/Papers/Entries/Simulating Urb.findings: The full SIGSPATIAL paper is available in the NSF Public Access Repository PDF (also indexed by the source search); its abstract agrees with the note. The `fulltext unavailable` flag and statement that only an abstract was accessible are inaccurate. The model summary is abstract-level and misses mechanisms explained in the paper, so extraction completeness cannot be affirmed. DOI/title/authors and zero imported reference links match the snapshot; `publication date: 2019` lacks month/day precision but matches conference year. Source-missingness error is the clear failure.

Literature/Papers/Entries/Social Agents-.findings: The full JASSS article/PDF was read, including review protocol and findings. The study-design claim (systematic review of 43 ABMs) is supported and correctly distinguishes the review from one unified simulation. The abstract has joined words at sentence boundaries (e.g. `ABMs).However`, `challenging.Here`) and thus is not an exact copy of publisher text. DOI, publication date, author list, tags and all 77 preserved references/order check out.

Literature/Papers/Entries/Social Relatio.findings: The full JASSS paper was read, including the model mechanics, strategy definitions, process schedule, and outcomes. The summary correctly identifies relationship development, trust-mediated formation/decay and strategy-spread outcomes, but it wrongly says the transition function and parameterization are unavailable because only the abstract was accessible. The full text specifies trust changes on cooperation/defection with nonlinear saturation and time decay; strategy-specific history-dependent partner search; alternating social and foraging turns; and measured tie distributions/fitness. Those defining rules and simplifications are omitted. DOI/date/title/authors and 62 preserved reference links/order check out.

Literature/Papers/Entries/Social Simulac.findings: The full UIST/arXiv paper was read, including the prompt pipeline and technical/user evaluations. The research questions and broad use as social-system design prototyping are supported. The Model section is too generic: source describes a prompt chain that expands example personas into a population, assigns profile attributes, generates interactions conditioned on community goal/rules/personas, and evaluates generated threads and design interventions. It also reports limits/validation conditions that the note leaves out. DOI, source, authors, date/tags and all 93 reference links/order check out. Claims that the method is not a promise of accurate prediction are a reasonable limitation but should be tied to the paper’s Discussion, not presented as an explicit author framing without qualification.

Literature/Papers/Entries/Social capital.findings: The full Nature article was read. Abstract is consistent with the published abstract; both Research Questions are supported, including the quasi-experimental cross-cohort and regression-discontinuity analyses of exposure and friending bias. Study-design summary correctly labels the paper empirical and describes the Facebook friendship analysis rather than a simulation. DOI, date, authors, tags and 51 preserved reference links/order check out.

Literature/Papers/Entries/Stochastic Act.primary_source_read: primary abstract/metadata read; full text blocked by publisher access
Literature/Papers/Entries/Stochastic Act.findings: The Annual Reviews publisher record provides the exact abstract and bibliographic metadata, which match the note. Full text did not load; the page requires institutional access. The model summary’s abstract-level statements are sound, but its footnotes claim support from specific model/coevolution sections that were not available for audit, and the note lacks `fulltext unavailable`. Mark the source limitation and avoid implying those sections were checked. DOI/date/authorship/tags and 112 preserved references/order check out.

Literature/Papers/Entries/T-RECS- A Simu.findings: The full arXiv paper was read, including framework design, simulation process and replication sections. It is a simulation framework, not one substantive behavioral model, but the note incorrectly says it does not prescribe components beyond reusable modules. The paper specifies an event-driven schedule, parallel user feedback handling, user preference/prediction and score state, optional preference evolution after exposure/consumption, dynamic or fixed items, creator incentives and metrics. The four model answers omit these defining framework rules; current claim that chosen studies alone supply behavioral assumptions is too broad. DOI/source/date/authors/tags and 62 preserved reference links/order check out.
